name.value: aversive classical conditioning with cognitive emotion regulation

description.value: Participants predicted the occurrence of an aversive picture after a conditioned stimulus while using either self-distancing or attentive observation.

spans.text: To investigate the effect of cognitive emotion regulation on emotional responses and learning, we conducted a model-based fMRI study in which the visual presentation of aversive stimuli was combined with classical conditioning and varying conditioned–unconditioned stimulus (CS–US) contingencies.
Distance
regulation strategy (‘Distance’ or ‘Attend’)

description.value: Participants actively down-regulated emotions elicited by aversive pictures using cognitive self-distancing, through self-focused and/or reality-focused distancing statements.

spans.text: In the Distance condition, participants were instructed to actively down-regulate emotions elicited by the negative pictures by means of cognitive self-distancing
Attend
regulation strategy (‘Distance’ or ‘Attend’)

description.value: Participants attentively observed the aversive pictures, allowed them to passively sink in, remained aware of their meaning, and were instructed not to alter the evoked emotions.

spans.text: In the Attend condition, participants were instructed to let the images passively sink in and to not alter the evoked emotions.
On each trial

Visual stimuli, presented with the Presentation software (Neurobehavioral Systems), were rear-projected on a screen at the head of the scanner and could be seen by participants through an adjustable mirror, mounted to a standard head coil.
A button press was required to predict whether a picture will follow or not

instructions.value: Participants predicted whether an aversive picture would follow each conditioned stimulus, used cognitive self-distancing to down-regulate emotions in the Distance condition, passively observed and did not alter emotions in the Attend condition, and rated emotional intensity after each trial.

spans.text: Participants were asked to indicate (predict) via a button press in the first 3 s of CS presentation whether a negative picture or no picture would follow the CS.

stimuli.value: Blue squares and yellow pentagons served as conditioned stimuli; aversive pictures from the International Affective Picture System served as unconditioned stimuli and were presented on 50% of trials, with blank screens on non-paired trials.

spans.text: The US, presented for 6 s, was a negative picture from the International Affective Picture System ( Lang et al., 1997 ), shown on 50% of the trials (Paired trials).

value: Prediction performance based on correlations between predicted and actual US occurrence, z-transformed across participants
Emotional intensity ratings on a -3 to 3 scale
Verbal reports confirming the emotion-regulation strategy used

spans.text: For a measure of prediction performance, behavioral predictions were correlated with the actual US presentation sequence for each participant resulting in Pearson's r values, z-transformed for comparison across participants
